function: Learned near-field beam training: a CNN (DBNS) predicts the optimal hybrid-field codeword index per subarray from subarray-wise far-field beam sweeps; non-learned VABR refines off-grid angle and distance (pp. 5-7).
system: Uplink XL-MIMO: BS ULA N=512 antennas, K=4 RF chains in partially-connected hybrid combiner, single-antenna user, near-field with spatial non-stationarity, 30 GHz, no RIS (pp. 3-4, 8).
method: Supervised residual CNN with K softmax heads, cross-entropy loss, labels from exhaustive-search codewords, 100 epochs; refinement VABR is non-learned (gradient ascent plus genetic algorithm) (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Custom simulation: one LoS and two NLoS near-field paths (Rician 10 dB) with Markov-chain visibility regions, random angles and distances; 10^5 training, 10^3 test realizations (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and test (N=512, K=4, eta=0.5); tests sweep SNR, top-X, eta (0.1-0.9) and K (2-32); training SNR and retraining not stated (pp. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: HFBS-sub, HFBS-full, FFBS-sub, THBT, GP-SOMP, GP-SIGW, perfect CSI. Learned: DNBT-SC, the earlier DNBT deep-learning beam training with top-X codewords (p. 9).
metrics: Normalized beamforming gain, beam prediction error probability, data rate, effective data rate including beam training time, beam training overhead (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Big-O for DBNS layers and for VABR, O(KN1((X+M)^2N2+M(X+M)(Np+NoNg))); overhead 6144 sweeps exhaustive versus 131 for DBNS; no runtime or parameter count (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "The channel between the BS and the user consists of one LoS path and L = 2 NLoS paths, where κ = 10 dB." Angles and distances are drawn at random and visibility regions follow a Markov chain (p. 3). Custom simulator: no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "The network is trained with a learning rate of 0.001" on 10^5 realizations of one setting (N = 512, K = 4, eta = 0.5). Figs. 4-9 (pp. 9-11) sweep SNR, X, eta and K, but the paper never says that the trained model was tested on conditions absent from training, or at which SNR it was trained.
q3_support: p. 9: "DNBT-SC: The method for predicting the optimal codeword by training a neural network using codeword samples from the hybrid-field codebook [16]." This is the earlier learned beam training method; non-learned baselines are HFBS-sub, HFBS-full, THBT, GP-SOMP and GP-SIGW (p. 9); all are compared on normalized gain and data rate (Figs. 4 and 9).
q4_support: p. 8: "the total computational complexity of the DBNS method can be calculated as" a Big-O in the layer sizes, and "the overall computational complexity of the VABR algorithm is given by" O(KN1((X+M)^2N2+M(X+M)(Np+NoNg))).
q5_support: p. 9: "All numerical results are obtained via Monte Carlo simulations"; channels are simulated, the paper gives no link or DOI for code or data and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Area 3 rather than 2: the learned DBNS predicts beam (codeword) indices and the metrics are normalized beamforming gain and data rate (pp. 9-11); the off-grid angle and distance estimation is done by VABR, which is not learned (p. 7), so it does not make this a learned channel estimator. q1: reference [33] (an extension of COST 2100) is cited for the visibility-region Markov chain (p. 3, p. 13), but the paper never says its simulator is built on COST 2100; the reviewer may confirm. q2: DBNS has K separate output paths (p. 6), so the sweep over K = 2 to 32 (Fig. 9, p. 11) needs a different network, and retraining for each condition does not count; no statement says one model was tested on unseen eta or SNR. q4 rests on the Big-O expressions of p. 8; the beam training overhead (6144 versus 131 sweeps) is signaling overhead and was not used.
